title: Laya vs BERTurk on Turkish banking intents: the frozen decision protocol (REP-01)

frozen.when: before any fine-tuned model is scored on test or HOTELS (REP-01, ROADMAP Phase 8 criterion 1)
frozen.why: every threshold, the seed-averaged bootstrap procedure and the few-shot protocol are fixed before a fine-tuned test number exists, so nothing can be tuned to the result
frozen.identity: the sha256 of this file's exact bytes, pinned in pilot.protocol.PROTOCOL_SHA256 by the freeze commit; every consumer calls pilot.protocol.require_frozen and refuses a missing or changed file

references.rule: reference rows are reported, never gated; their θ is D-12 on their own committed val dump; majority and prior are not scored on hotels_probe; zero-shot Laya is scored once on hotels_probe as an ungated reference OOD row, on the scorer of its committed val dump (cpu, Ray workers 2 x 4 CPUs; A15)

scoring.once: each final seed is scored once per split into results/dumps/<dump_run_id>/<split>; an existing dump is never replaced
refused: a device or worker count other than this block's
a manifest other than the committed data/splits.json
scoring.why: mps, fp32, in-process: the scorer of the val dumps the postfit T and θ were fitted on (A14)

variant.headline: each final seed's shipped T (= its postfit record's T) with the record's theta.shipped (global plus per-tag, pilot.metrics.theta_vector); every gating number uses it (A18)
variant.raw: T = 1 with the record's theta.raw; reported only, never gating
variant.references: majority, prior and zero-shot Laya keep D-12 on their own val dump (pilot.metrics.select_theta)

seed_averaging.rule: per seed s, P_s = sigmoid(logit_s / T_s) with T_s the record T; P = the mean over the 3 seeds per message and tag (pilot.metrics.seed_average); θ = the record's theta.shipped (global plus per-tag, theta_vector) applied to P; probabilities are averaged before any threshold, never metrics (EVAL-07, A5)
seed_averaging.raw: the same with T_s = 1 and the record's theta.raw; reported only
seed_averaging.theta_source: the postfit record's θ, chosen on val by one selection seed; a final seed has no clean val (final_train holds the val folds), so θ is never re-selected on the final seeds or on test

bootstrap.procedure: EVAL-07: a paired message-level bootstrap of Laya - BERTurk over the seed-averaged probabilities of each system; one index draw (pilot.metrics.bootstrap_weights(n, B, seed)) is shared by both systems and by every metric; each replicate's delta is computed at each system's fixed θ; the interval is the percentile interval of the replicate deltas; replicates where a delta is undefined are counted and left out
bootstrap.extra: the draw is bootstrap_weights(n, B, seed), the same one paired_bootstrap uses, shared by both systems; Brier and classwise ECE replicates are count-weighted sums of per-message terms, so each equals the metric of the resampled rows; a precision-at-coverage replicate is selective on the rows idx[b] in draw order (stable ties follow draw order); the interval is the percentile interval of the replicate deltas A - B (percentile (numpy linear interpolation))

a.name: non-inferiority
a.rule: PASS when the micro-F1 delta 95% CI lower bound >= micro_ci_lower_min and the macro-F1 delta point estimate >= macro_point_min; FAIL when the micro-F1 delta CI upper bound < micro_fail_ci_upper_below or the macro-F1 delta point estimate < macro_point_min; INCONCLUSIVE otherwise. The macro-F1 CI is reported with macro_ci_label, not gated; deltas are Laya - BERTurk fractions in [0, 1] (points = fraction x 100), compared unrounded
a.macro_ci_label: not resolvable at this test size (n = 413)

b.name: seeds and no collapsed run
b.rule: PASS when no run the collapse rule applies to is collapsed and every model has exactly seeds_per_model distinct scored final seeds; FAIL otherwise

c.name: latency
c.rule: per-message latency of every final seed is reported, not gated, in v1 (a budget is DEC-01, v2)
c.label: reported, not gated

d.name: a clear edge on calibration, abstention or few-shot learning
d.rule: PASS when any one path is MET; PENDING when none is MET and the few-shot path is pending; FAIL otherwise. calibration: the Brier delta < delta_below and its CI upper bound < ci_upper_below; abstention: the precision at coverage % delta >= delta_at_least and its CI lower bound > ci_lower_above; fewshot: the mean over draws of the new-tag macro-AP delta at k >= mean_delta_at_least (PENDING until Phase 9); deltas are Laya - BERTurk fractions in [0, 1] (points = fraction x 100), compared unrounded

reported_only.classwise_ece: reported, not gated (A1): its percentile bootstrap is biased (binned ECE replicates are inflated, so the observed delta sat at the 93.8th percentile of its own replicates on val; Roelofs et al., AISTATS 2022) and its direction flips between T = 1 and the fitted T; Brier names the calibration path

alternative_go.name: alternative GO
alternative_go.rule: MET when the micro-F1 delta > delta_above and its 95% CI lower bound > ci_lower_above; it gives GO only with (b) PASS; deltas are Laya - BERTurk fractions in [0, 1] (points = fraction x 100), compared unrounded

collapse.rule: a run is collapsed when any component applied to it is collapsed; (b) needs no collapsed run

applies_to.runs: the selection run of each model

applies_to.source: its final-manifest entry and its test dump

val_floor.rule: collapsed when the chosen candidate's val micro-F1 at its global val θ after T, the exact fraction 2TP / (2TP + FP + FN) of the record's objective counts, is strictly below the label prior's val micro-F1 at the prior's own global val θ (prior_val_fraction); equal is not collapsed

loss.rule: collapsed when any epoch's mean training loss is NaN or infinite, or the last epoch's is strictly above the first epoch's (divergent); equal is not collapsed
loss.note: the per-epoch loss is the unweighted mean over micro-batches (Laya) or steps (BERTurk); Laya's RLCD sigma anneal makes its epochs not strictly comparable, but the rule still catches a blow-up

test_floor.rule: collapsed when a final seed's test micro-F1 at its record's global shipped θ, the exact fraction 2TP / (2TP + FP + FN), is strictly below the label prior's test micro-F1 at the prior's global val θ (prior_test_fraction); equal is not collapsed
test_floor.addition: Claude-recommended addition to the REP-01 default, frozen before any fine-tuned test number (08-RESEARCH Open Question 1)

collapse.not_applied: the val floor is not applied to final seeds: final_train holds the val folds
collapse.prior_source: results/dumps/prior/{val,test}: the label prior at T = 1; θ = its global val θ (pilot.metrics.select_theta); micro-F1 = 2TP / (2TP + FP + FN) over all 48 tags

rules: (a) INCONCLUSIVE -> INCONCLUSIVE (counts as NO-GO; collect bank data)
(a) PASS and (d) PENDING -> PROVISIONAL: the verdict is computed with the few-shot path of (d) MET and NOT MET; it is final when both agree
verdict.inconclusive_means: counts as NO-GO; collect bank data
verdict.provisional: PROVISIONAL: %s if the few-shot path of (d) is met, else %s
verdict.units: deltas are Laya - BERTurk fractions in [0, 1] (points = fraction x 100), compared unrounded

definitions.brier: mean over every (message, tag) pair of (p - y)^2; the per-message sum over 48 tags is 48 x this
definitions.nll: mean binary cross-entropy over every (message, tag) pair, p clipped to [1e-12, 1 - 1e-12]
definitions.classwise_ece: Kull et al. 2019 Eq. 4: per tag, the sum over the 15 equal-width bins of |sum of y - sum of p| / n; averaged over all 48 tags, zero-support tags included
definitions.bins: 15 equal-width bins [k/15, (k+1)/15), p = 1.0 in the last bin (Guo et al. 2017, M = 15)
definitions.confidence: message confidence = sum over the 48 tags of log q, q = p if p >= θ (predicted) else 1 - p: the model's probability that every tag decision is right, assuming tag independence
definitions.coverage: keep the k = ceil(c * n / 100) most confident messages, k computed as (c * n + 99) // 100; ties in confidence keep split-file order (stable sort)
definitions.aurc: mean over k = 1..n of 1 - exact-match rate of the k most confident messages (Geifman et al. 2019); lower is better
definitions.theta_tie: closest to 0.5; between two equally close points, the lower θ
definitions.bootstrap_extra: the draw is bootstrap_weights(n, B, seed), the same one paired_bootstrap uses, shared by both systems; Brier and classwise ECE replicates are count-weighted sums of per-message terms, so each equals the metric of the resampled rows; a precision-at-coverage replicate is selective on the rows idx[b] in draw order (stable ties follow draw order); the interval is the percentile interval of the replicate deltas A - B (percentile (numpy linear interpolation))
definitions.false_positive: a counted message has no gold tag among the scored columns; it is a false positive when at least one scored column is predicted at θ (P >= θ). No-intent: all 48 columns. Out-of-domain: the 22 banking-only columns (the manifest's ood_scoring_tags)
definitions.average_precision: average precision of one tag: AP = sum over the distinct score thresholds, in decreasing order, of (R_n - R_(n-1)) * P_n, with P_n and R_n the precision and recall of the messages scoring at or above the n-th threshold; tied scores form one threshold; not interpolated (sklearn average_precision_score); a tag with no positive is refused; T-invariant (a monotone transform of the logits keeps the ranking)
definitions.fewshot_sampler: rows sorted by uid; one random.Random(seed) per draw (CPython 3.12 random); for each tag in TAGS order: rng.sample of max(k) positives from the sorted uids carrying the tag, then rng.sample of NEG_PER_POS x max(k) negatives from the sorted uids without it; the k support set is the union over tags of the first k positives and the first NEG_PER_POS x k negatives (in sample order), so the k = 5 set is nested in the k = 10 set; replay = rng.sample of REPLAY from the sorted uids outside the max-k support set; every stored list is sorted; a pool smaller than a draw needs is refused, never shortened
definitions.fewshot_digest: sha256 of the compact (separators ',' and ':'), key-sorted, UTF-8 JSON of {"schema", "seed", "tags", "support": {k: sorted uids}, "replay": sorted uids}; k keys are strings

rule.banking_only: every held-out tag is in pilot.pins.OOD_SCORING_TAGS

eligibility.note: gold labels only, no model output: positives per held-out tag in the committed test and final_train splits

sampler.rule: rows sorted by uid; one random.Random(seed) per draw (CPython 3.12 random); for each tag in TAGS order: rng.sample of max(k) positives from the sorted uids carrying the tag, then rng.sample of NEG_PER_POS x max(k) negatives from the sorted uids without it; the k support set is the union over tags of the first k positives and the first NEG_PER_POS x k negatives (in sample order), so the k = 5 set is nested in the k = 10 set; replay = rng.sample of REPLAY from the sorted uids outside the max-k support set; every stored list is sorted; a pool smaller than a draw needs is refused, never shortened
sampler.digest: sha256 of the compact (separators ',' and ':'), key-sorted, UTF-8 JSON of {"schema", "seed", "tags", "support": {k: sorted uids}, "replay": sorted uids}; k keys are strings

base_runs.rule: one label-masked base run per model and seed on selection_train (folds 0-13, so val stays held out for the bases' θ) at the model's chosen recipe: Laya ray_train.py --epochs 4 --stop-after-epoch 3, neg 8, encoder LR 2e-05, head LR 1e-4, mps, one worker; BERTurk berturk_train.py --epochs 30 --stop-after-epoch 29, LR 2e-05, head LR 1e-4, batch 32, mps fp32; seeds 0, 1, 2, base seed d paired with draw d; the same recipe as the main experiment, so the comparison isolates the masking

rules.masking: every selection_train message is kept; the six held-out tags are removed from each row's expected before neg8 sampling for Laya (laya.train.items_from_rows skips a question with no expected entry, so the base sees no item of them) and set to pilot.berturk.MASK_LABEL -100 for BERTurk (masked BCE: zero gradient); the masked base sees no label of the six tags (Phase 9 proves it: base items per held-out question = 0, unmasked BERTurk labels in those columns = 0)

new_question.laya: the masked tag's existing intents.py question, QUESTIONS[tag] ({"type": "noul", "instructions": INTENTS[tag]}), never reworded: questions_sha256 is frozen in data/splits.json and a wording change refreezes every split; the base never sees it because items_from_rows skips a question without an expected entry
new_question.berturk: the base's own classifier row for the tag, trained on no label (masked BCE gives it zero gradient; weight decay only); no weight imprinting (XCMP-04 is v2)

rules.support_labels: every support message carries its full gold labels for all 48 tags; the support set of a k is the union over the six tags of their k positives and 4k negatives; the realised positive count of each new tag per k is reported: it can exceed k, through co-occurrence and because a negative drawn for one tag may carry another held-out tag (negatives lack only their own tag)
rules.replay: 200 selection_train messages outside the draw's k = 10 support set (the same replay set for k = 5 and k = 10), with old-tag labels only: the six new tags are masked as in the base runs

continued_training.rule: 10 epochs from the masked base of seed = draw seed at the base LRs (encoder 2e-05, head 1e-4), on the support set plus the replay set, each trainer's own schedule over the 10 epochs (Laya cosine and sigma anneal, BERTurk linear with 10% warm-up), training seed = draw seed, no early stopping, no selection on val or test; epoch parity, not step parity, disclosed: BERTurk takes about 160 optimizer steps against Laya's about 2,000

rules.laya_item_rule: support rows: every positive, every label of the six new tags (positive or negative) and 8 random old-tag negatives; replay rows: neg8 over the 42 old tags; plain neg8 would drop most new-tag negatives; the asymmetry with BERTurk's full labels is disclosed as in the main experiment (neg8 against all 48 labels)

primary_metric.rule: per new tag, average precision on test by pilot.metrics.AP_RULE on P = sigmoid(logit) (T-invariant: raw T = 1); macro-AP = mean over the six tags; the aggregate is the mean over the three draws; criterion (d) reads the mean over draws of (Laya - BERTurk) macro-AP at k = 10; k = 5 is reported

secondary_metrics: k = 0 new-tag macro-AP of each masked base (Laya answers the new question zero-shot; BERTurk's untrained row)
new-tag micro-F1 and 42-old-tag micro-F1 at the masked base's val θ (the val rule at T = 1)
forgetting: old-tag micro-F1 of the continued model minus the masked base's
a paired message-level bootstrap CI of the new-tag macro-AP delta (descriptive only)
incremental wall clock per continued-training run

compute_fallback.rule: 1 masked base run per model (seed 0), all three draws continued from it
compute_fallback.trigger: the Phase 9 projection from the results/compute rates exceeds 10 h, or a primary base run still fails after the LAYA-03 ladder
compute_fallback.disclosure: the results state that base-model variance is not captured

rules.gate: the few-shot runner calls pilot.protocol.require_frozen() before anything else and records protocol_sha256 in every Phase 9 record
rules.test_admission: a few-shot checkpoint reaches test only through the score.py protocol gate, once Phase 9 binds its run record to this protocol_sha256 and a draw digest; Phase 8's allow-list holds the six final seeds only
phase_9_notes: ray_train.py has no tag masking: add --mask-tags (an IDENTITY key dropped when None), applied to expected before spike.neg8_rows
berturk_train.py refuses continued training from a fine-tuned head (optimizer_groups requires a newly initialised head): add a continued-training mode
support sets are not registered splits: both trainers need a protocol-derived support-set source over the verified selection_train bytes; data/splits.json is never refrozen

known_at_freeze.note: in-sample val: T, θ and the epoch were chosen on these 208 messages, by one selection seed per model, while the test system is a 3-seed average; the thresholds are the REP-01 defaults, written before any result, and are not tuned to these numbers; both (d) paths (Brier, precision at 80% coverage) favour BERTurk on val and (a) sits near the margin; recorded so that what was known at freeze time is disclosed

power_context.label: research estimate, normal approximation (A19): 08-RESEARCH CI-width research, from the in-sample val deltas (B = 10,000, seed 0) scaled to the test size; the 3-seed average makes the SE somewhat smaller
power_context.p_a_lower_note: P(the (a) micro-F1 delta CI lower bound >= -0.02) at a true micro-F1 delta of each key; -0.0155 is the in-sample val estimate
power_context.margin_80_power_note: the non-inferiority margin with 80% power at a true delta of 0
power_context.alternative_go_note: P(the alternative GO is MET) at a true micro-F1 delta of each key
power_context.margin: the -0.02 margin is locked (REP-01) and kept; (a) is three-way, so a non-resolvable result reads INCONCLUSIVE, which counts as NO-GO plus collect bank data
